**My reasoning, as myself:**

I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My son went to Shijiazhuang years ago, so now it's mostly me. I have 5 mu of contracted land. I can't do everything by hand anymore — I hire the machine-plowing service from the village and the combine comes at harvest. That's just how it works now.

I grow wheat and maize. That's what I've always grown, that's what my neighbors grow, that's what the seed shop and the fertilizer shop are set up for. I don't have the energy or the money to try cotton or vegetables — that needs more attention and I don't know those markets.

In October, after I bring in the maize, I'll have the rotary tiller come and prepare the ground, then seed the wheat. I buy seed from the township cooperative — the improved variety they recommend, not the old seeds my mother kept. Better yields. For maize in June, I always buy hybrid seed. Everyone does.

Fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer at base and top up with urea in spring when the wheat starts growing. My neighbor told me I use too much nitrogen, but I'd rather not lose the harvest over trying to save a few yuan on urea.

I water the wheat four times — at sowing (if dry), in early spring when it resumes growing, at jointing, and at heading. Maize I water at planting and once more in August if it's hot. Summer rains help.

Pesticides: spring herbicide for the wheat, then aphid spray before harvest. For maize, herbicide right after it comes up. That's usually enough.
